newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Telfort, EnerTel win Dutch fixed-phone licences.
newsitem.headline: Telfort, EnerTel win Dutch fixed-phone licences.

text.p: The Dutch minister for transport and waterways expects to award two terrestrial telecoms licences to operators EnerTel and Telfort in the next month, the ministry announced on Wednesday.
The two operators will provide competition to the current fixed-line monopoly of Dutch PTT (Koninklijke PTT Nederland).
Three groups submitted applications in September for licences to build and operate national fixed-line public telephone networks in the Netherlands.
Telfort is a joint venture between British Telecom Plc and state-owned Dutch Railways (NS).
Enertel is a consortium of Dutch regional power companies and local cable television network operators.

An application from Global One, a joint venture of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom, was unsuccessful as it failed to meet one of the government's conditions, the ministry said. It declined to identify the condition.
